summary:
Turn 46 reviewed the dead-rejection-path check, whose outcome is violated.

State on entry. Claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection has one artifact, 374c3ca1233e4a00af8a1f18626ea9db (executed as 1da81676…), with outcome violated and oracle correspondence unreviewed. Its retained stream prints accept_reply_higher_ballot with reply_ballot 5 against the round's last_tried_ballot 3, nacks 0, prepare_sent false and the status unchanged. Claim C6 was also confirmed this cycle, so the promoted-leader variant of the recovery divergence is settled too.

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a reply whose ballot exceeds the accept round's ballot must be recorded as a rejection so the leader can make a new ballot and prepare again, and the predicate asserts nacks == 1, evaluated on the handler's own counters — the run reports 0, so the assertion is genuinely tested rather than filtered. Entry and legality: the round is built with the package's own instance and bookkeeping constructors in the state a leader reaches after the accept branch (ACCEPTED with the round's ballot), and the reply is the value handleAccept sends when its stored bal exceeds the accept ballot, so both sides are implementation-produced. Oracle and identity: the counters read after the call are the handler's bookkeeping values and the round and reply events share instance 1.0. Observation path and completion: the handler is synchronous and nothing later is claimed, so no wait or cleanup duty is implied. Contrary evidence and the bounded consequence: the pre-accept side cannot produce a differing reply at all (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so this handler holds the only rejection branch — and the 10s execution timeout can still drive the instance into recovery, which is why the claim is scoped as a delay on the collision path rather than a stall. The limitations record that the timeout path is not exercised, that only one reply is delivered so the majority-nack consequence is not reached, and that the round is constructed rather than driven.

Frontier. Seven claims are now settled (C1 recovery divergence, C2 stable-store record, C3 applied-state divergence, C4 the NOOP-commit crash, C5 the owner-alive re-proposal protection, C6 the promoted-leader variant, C7 the dead accept-rejection path pending this review); the two paused candidates keep their resume conditions, and the remaining visible items are the scope-issue bookkeeping on the superseded C1 artifact and the unread helper surfaces. No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
